alex_support: FYI customer (AcmeMaps) reporting sporadic tail latency spikes on /v1/embeddings and intermittent "dimension" errors. Started after they bumped client-side max_batch_size -> 512. Repro + logs pasted below, need SRE/eng help :disappointed_relieved:

maria_sre: Can you paste a sample request_id / trace_id and the region? Also is this happening for a single route/model?

alex_support: trace_id=trace-0a1b2c3d region=us-west-2 route=embeddings-semantic-1536. Errors ~0.3% of requests, p99 jumps to ~3s from usual ~120ms during the window. Repro curl below + a short server log excerpt.

alex_support: ```
# minimal curl repro (customer reported)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"sem-1536","inputs":["short text 1","short text 2"]}'
```

alex_support: logs: ```
[2026-02-28T14:12:03Z] batcher: coalesced 7 reqs -> batch_size=128
[2026-02-28T14:12:03Z] batcher: pad applied total_tokens=8192
[2026-02-28T14:12:03Z] model-check: dimension-check failed: expected 1536, got 6144 (request=trace-0a1b2c3d)
[2026-02-28T14:12:03Z] response: 400 invalid_input_shape (req=trace-0a1b2c3d)
```

tyler_ml: quick Qs: are clients sending a flattened vector for each item or a nested array? That error (expected 1536, got 6144) looks like a shape-length mismatch (6144 == 1536 * 4). Could be four concatenated items or a mis-declared batch dimension. Also curious if they enabled any client-side packing or pre-batching.

alex_support: customer says their SDK batcher merges many tiny requests; they thought bumping max_batch_size would help throughput. Example of their python change: ```python
# they switched from per-item send to:
client.max_batch_size = 512
for item in items:
    client.enqueue(item)
```
They did not change the payload shaping code.

maria_sre: hypothesis: dynamic batching + large max_batch_size -> more aggressive coalescing -> higher pad/kv-cache flushes -> occasional expensive allocations and shape confusion when per-request metadata gets dropped. Need traces + full request payload to be sure. Query suggestion: get p50/p95/p99 for "embeddings-semantic-1536" grouped by request_size and by client_id. Dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/embeddings/sem-1536?window=1h

alex_support: pulled metrics: p50=120ms, p95=210ms, p99=3.1s during spike window. 90% of offending traces came from client_id=acmemaps, request_items=4-12 (tiny requests) that got coalesced into very large batches. I also attached a sample raw request body (they accidentally flattened arrays when they reimplemented the batching): ```json
{"model":"sem-1536","inputs":[[0.1,0.2,...], [0.3,0.4,...]]}
```
(note: they sent flattened lists rather than arrays with explicit shape metadata per item which confused a downstream validation check when coalesced)

tyler_ml: ok that explains the dimension error. Root cause appears to be malformed per-item shape combined with aggressive coalescing. Two actions: 1) short-term mitigation: ask customer to set client.max_batch_size back to 128 or disable client packing; server-side: set `coalesce_window_ms: 25` and `max_batch_size: 128` for the route to reduce risk while we patch. 2) longer-term: add stricter input-shape validation at the batcher boundary (emit original per-request item lengths into logs so we can catch which item caused mismatch).

evan_engineer: I'll open runtime ticket (RT-8452) and attach traces/logs + example payload. Provisional patch: validate per-request length hash before coalescing and drop/return 400 with clearer message instead of letting model-check fail later; also emit a metric `batcher.malformed_item_count`. Patch will be small but we need a canary. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Created ticket RT-8452 and assigned to eng-runtime (priority=P2).

alex_support: great — I'll inform AcmeMaps and provide the workaround (roll back to 128, add coalesce_window tweak). Repro steps and curl snips copied to the ticket. Will follow up once runtime confirms canary. Thanks all.

maria_sre: optional: if we see tail latency still high after max_batch_size rollback, collect heap/alloc samples during spike and the per-shard queue lengths.

alex_support: noted, will collect if needed. Closing loop on support side once RT-8452 shows progress.
